title: Visitors and sick contacts: protecting your newborn
summary: Newborns have developing immune systems. Boundaries are health care, not rudeness.
whatsNormal:
It is reasonable to limit exposure in the early weeks.

• Ask visitors to wash hands before holding baby
• Skip visits from anyone with fever, cough, cold sores, or vomiting
• Kissing baby on hands or feet instead of face reduces germ spread
• Older siblings at daycare bring home viruses, extra hand washing helps
• Outdoor or distanced visits can still share joy safely

You do not owe everyone immediate access. Your pediatrician supports protective choices.
watchFor: Baby fever 100.4°F (38°C) or higher if under 3 months after a sick contact
Runny nose with poor feeding or unusual sleepiness
Cold sore (herpes) lesion near baby, newborn herpes is an emergency
Cough in baby or breathing faster than usual
callDoctorIf: Any fever in a baby under 3 months, call now
Baby exposed to someone with active cold sores and you see lesions on baby
Breathing difficulty, blue lips, or dehydration signs
You want guidance after a known exposure, nurse lines can triage
